constants: An object of signal, error-number, and process-priority constants.
EOL: The platform-specific end-of-line marker. `'\r\n'` on Windows, `'\n'` everywhere else.
devNull: The platform-specific path to the null device. `'\\\\.\\nul'` on Windows, `'/dev/null'` everywhere else.
platform: Returns the operating system platform as a string. Possible values include `'android'`, `'darwin'`, `'ios'`, `'linux'`, and `'win32'`.
arch: Returns the CPU architecture as a string. Possible values include `'arm'`, `'arm64'`, `'ia32'`, and `'x64'`.
type: Returns the operating system name as returned by `uname(3)`.
machine: Returns the machine type as a string.
execPath: Returns the absolute path of the executable that started the process.
chdir: Changes the current working directory to `dir`.
tmpdir: Returns the operating system's default directory for temporary files.
homedir: Returns the home directory of the current user.
hostname: Returns the hostname of the operating system.
networkInterfaces: Returns an object containing network interfaces that have been assigned a network address. Each key on the returned object identifies a network interface.
kill: Sends `signal` to the process identified by `pid`. `signal` can be a string or a number. Defaults to `'SIGTERM'`.
userInfo: Returns information about a current user. The `uid` value defaults to the current effective uid.
groupInfo: Returns information about a group. The `gid` value defaults to the effective group ID of the calling process.
endianness: Returns `'LE'` on little-endian systems and `'BE'` on big-endian systems.
availableParallelism: Returns the number of logical CPU cores available to the process.
cpuUsage: Returns an object with `user` and `system` properties, each representing CPU time in microseconds. If `previous` is provided, the returned values are relative to it.
threadCpuUsage: Like `os.cpuUsage()` but for the current thread only.
resourceUsage: Returns an object describing the resource usage of the current process.
memoryUsage: Returns an object describing the memory usage of the process.
freemem: Returns the amount of free system memory in bytes.
totalmem: Returns the total amount of system memory in bytes.
availableMemory: Returns an estimate of the amount of memory available for the process in bytes.
constrainedMemory: Returns the amount of memory available to the process under resource constraints, such as cgroups.
uptime: Returns the system uptime in seconds.
loadavg: Returns an array containing the 1, 5, and 15 minute load averages.
cpus: Returns an array of objects describing each logical CPU core.
setProcessTitle: Sets the process title. `title` is coerced to a string and must be shorter than 256 characters.
getPriority: Returns the scheduling priority of the process specified by `pid`. Defaults to `0`, meaning the current process.
setPriority: Sets the scheduling priority of the process specified by `pid`. If `pid` is omitted, the priority of the current process is set.
getEnvKeys: Returns an array of the names of all environment variables.
getEnv: Returns the value of the environment variable `name`, or `undefined` if it is not set.
hasEnv: Returns `true` if the environment variable `name` is set, otherwise `false`.
